EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  October 23, 2017

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Susan Brtis
Lou Persichina
Bill Kemp
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director
Mike Whitehead, Administrative Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 25, 2017

MEMBER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE SEPTEMBER 25, 2017 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
None.

PARK SECURITY CAMERAS UPDATE
The Administrative Services Director reported that he had received one proposal and quote
for placing cameras within Ernie Howlett Park and was expecting another this week. The first
quote was over $100,000 to provide full coverage of Howlett Park. In response to inquiries
regarding placing cameras in Chandler Park, he stated that during a park tour earlier that day,
he developed a project estimate of $3,000 to run conduit into the park, two cameras at a total
cost of $4,000, technical costs (update City’s server, digital recording storage, and a back-up
unit) costing $5,000, and a tall pole to mount the cameras for a undetermined cost.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
OCTOBER 23, 2017  1
 MEMBER SHINN inquired about the objectives of placing an expensive camera system in
Chandler Park when there were only a few Horse Trainers violating the rules. CHAIRMAN
SCHMITZ responded that installing cameras in all the City parks was a goal of City Council
and would eliminate the costs of placing a Code Enforcement Officer in Chandler Park to
monitor arena regulations compliance. The Administrative Services Director noted that the
cameras would also livestream activities taking place in our parks, so that residents could
determine whether an area of a park was in use and also provide day and night security
surveillance. In addition, he noted that the video tapes could be utilized when claims against
the City were filed for incidents in the City’s parks.
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO RECOMMEND THAT PLACEMENT OF A CAMERA SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM IN
  CHANDLER PARK BE MADE A PRIORITY BY CITY COUNCIL.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

CHANDLER PARK ARENA FOOTING PROJECT
The Community Services Director reported that the project had started, as planned, earlier
that morning with grading company, Mike Drews Construction utilizing a laser grader device.
He noted that the low settlement spots in the arena were notable and likely due to the park
being developed originally with uncompacted fill soil material. The arena renovation project is
expected to be completed by Friday of that week.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

PV WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE
The Community Services Director indicated that there was little to report on this project at this
time. He had contacted Angie Gilbride from California Water Service Company and Nancy
Wildman from the Palomino Homeowners Association, who had nothing to report. Gil Houle,
Peter Weber Equestrian Center Concessionaire, indicated that he was still collecting
proposals and quotes for up to 20 covered pipe corrals proposed to be temporarily installed
on an adjacent portion of the Palos Verdes Landfill.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
There were no issues to report since the September 25, 2017 Equestrian Committee meeting.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
OCTOBER 23, 2017  2
 COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  There were no public trail or arena issues reported. The Community Services Director
  reported that the Dapplegray Lanes Property Owners Association was having issues
  regarding the restriction of vehicles on its private trails and may be a future agenda
  item. MEMBER SHINN informed the Committee that Lomita Feed was seeking a
  buyer.

B.  EQUESTRIAN/PEDESTRIAN STREET CROSSINGS PROJECT UPDATE
  The Community Services Director reported that the Assistant City Manager was
  assured by the project contractor that work would start up again this week and was
  expected to be completed by next week.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT UPDATE

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 7:24 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
